_comment: Human-reviewed license register. Each entry records what a reviewer verified. Any change in version, scope, license or license-file hash fails `scripts/license_audit.py check` until re-reviewed. accepted_issues may only acknowledge known, reviewed gaps.

native.distribution: Not redistributed: frameworks are part of macOS and are resolved at load time
native.license: Apple SDK / macOS license (proprietary, part of the OS)
native.name: Apple system frameworks (CryptoKit, Foundation, LocalAuthentication, Security)
native.notes: No third-party source or binary code is copied into the helper.
native.use: Linked dynamically by native/macos/se-helper/main.swift via -framework flags in build.sh

native.distribution: Helper binary is built locally by the operator (build.sh) and is not included in the wheel or sdist
native.name: Swift standard library and runtime
native.notes: Evidence (session 13): the helper built by build.sh (sha256 a6fdd469..., matches the operator pin) links only OS-provided Swift libraries in /usr/lib/swift (libswiftCore, libswiftFoundation overlays, etc., per otool -L); no Swift runtime is copied into the binary. Upstream LICENSE.txt at tag swift-6.4.2-RELEASE (sha256 770af8291f708538d8ff885a0bbc4e045cd700531741c4f99528d435c14d7f55; toolchain reports Apple Swift 6.4.2) is Apache-2.0 with a Runtime Library Exception: portions embedded by compilation may be redistributed without the attribution of sections 4(a), 4(b) and 4(d). Conclusion: the helper is not distributed; if it ever is, no Swift attribution is required for compiler-embedded code, and the OS-provided runtime is not shipped.
native.use: The helper is compiled with xcrun swiftc; on macOS 14+ the Swift runtime is part of the OS

native.name: Xcode command-line tools (swiftc, codesign, shasum)
native.notes: Build requirement, not a component of the output.

cffi.attribution: MIT-0 needs no attribution; the MIT-licensed cffi/_cffi_gen_src.py requires its copyright and permission notice to be kept in copies or substantial portions (reproduced in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES).
cffi.notes: Evidence (session 13): wheel METADATA License-Expression MIT-0, LICENSE text MIT No Attribution (RECORD-verified); sdist cffi-2.1.1.tar.gz downloaded, sha256 matches uv.lock. Per-file scan of the installed wheel found one file under a different license: cffi/_cffi_gen_src.py, integrated from cffi-buildtool, MIT License, Copyright (c) 2024 Rose Davidson; its notice is reproduced in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. The sdist also carries vendored libffi 3.4.2 sources (MIT-style, Anthony Green and Red Hat) under src/c/libffi_*; on macOS the extension links the system /usr/lib/libffi.dylib (otool -L), so libffi is not embedded in the macOS wheel. Windows wheels may embed libffi; not verified here. Effective terms for the macOS wheel: MIT-0 AND MIT.

colorama.attribution: Not distributed by Sentinel (Windows-only development dependency).
colorama.notes: Evidence (session 13): not installed on macOS (only required when sys_platform == 'win32', dev-only via pytest). Verified from artifacts instead: wheel colorama-0.4.6-py2.py3-none-any.whl and sdist colorama-0.4.6.tar.gz downloaded from PyPI, both sha256 match uv.lock. METADATA has no License-Expression; classifier 'License :: OSI Approved :: BSD License'; LICENSE.txt (sha256 cac35c02686e5d04a5a7140bfb3b36e73aed496656e891102e428886d7930318, identical in wheel) is 'Copyright (c) 2010 Jonathan Hartley' with three conditions including non-endorsement, which matches the BSD-3-Clause template (reviewer judgment from the text). Not distributed by Sentinel.

cryptography.attribution: Sentinel does not redistribute cryptography; it is installed from PyPI. A redistributor of cryptography's binary wheel must keep cryptography's LICENSE, LICENSE.APACHE and LICENSE.BSD and OpenSSL's Apache-2.0 license (Apache-2.0 section 4); Rust crate licenses (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-3-Clause) also require their notices when redistributed in binary form.
embedded: OpenSSL 3.5.6, statically linked: Apache-2.0 (upstream LICENSE.txt, sha256 7d5450cb2d142651b8afa315b5f238efc805dad827d91ba367d8516bc9d49e7a)

Rust crates per sdist Cargo.lock (36 registry crates, crates.io-declared licenses: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, MIT OR Apache-2.0, Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, (MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Unicode-3.0)
cryptography.notes: Evidence (session 13): wheel METADATA License-Expression 'Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause' and its three license files (RECORD-verified); sdist cryptography-46.0.7.tar.gz downloaded from PyPI, sha256 matches uv.lock, same expression and files. Embedded: OpenSSL is statically linked (otool -L shows no libssl/libcrypto dependency; the binary reports 'OpenSSL 3.5.6 7 Apr 2026'); OpenSSL 3.5.6 LICENSE.txt fetched from the upstream openssl-3.5.6 tag is Apache-2.0 and is reproduced in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES; upstream has no NOTICE file at that tag (HTTP 404), nor does cryptography 46.0.7. Rust crates: the 36 registry crates in the sdist's Cargo.lock were checked against crates.io (all checksums match); declared licenses are all permissive: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, MIT OR Apache-2.0, 'Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception' (target-lexicon, build-time only) and '(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Unicode-3.0' (unicode-ident, used by proc macros at build time). Crate license texts were not individually copied; crates.io metadata is the declared license, not verified text.
